perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He is a police officer. Jonathan is his childhood best friend; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice on personal and professional matters and values his perspective.
- Christian has felt that Jonathan is hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious. He decided to confront Jonathan and arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan say Christian could trust him, then admit there was something: Jonathan was in trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered help, saying they could face it together. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, then that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He felt conflicted and concerned but decided to investigate discreetly. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but did not do anything illegal himself. Christian said he would look into it discreetly; Jonathan said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe/learn that Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan this. He heard Jonathan ask if he was sure and who would do it. Christian said he was not sure yet but had leads and would gather more evidence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later believed/knew the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it and that it was someone they both knew and trusted. He heard Jonathan express disbelief, warn that the person was dangerous, and say he trusted Christian to do what was right. Christian decided to confront the real culprit and bring them to justice.
